track_a.title: Displaced Yes checkbox
track_a.explanation: The Yes box moves 24 PDF points right and misses its reference box. The incident field then loses correspondence, taking its section, role and applicability matches with it.

track_a.title: Swapped option ownership
track_a.explanation: The boxes stay in place, but the prediction assigns Yes to the printed No box and No to the printed Yes box. The incident field fails the joint field check.

track_a.title: Missing section membership
track_a.explanation: The prediction leaves incident details outside the Applicant section. Its answer box is still present. Four of the five reference memberships are recovered.

track_a.title: Lost Business Office assignment
track_a.explanation: The prediction removes the role from the Business Office section. Reviewer name and review date inherit the default Applicant role, leaving three correct assignments out of five.

track_a.title: Reversed applicability condition
track_a.explanation: The reference activates incident details on Yes. The prediction activates it on No. The target field is correct, but the only applicability rule fails the truth-table comparison.

track_b.title: Accepted omission
track_b.explanation: The reference records the reviewer as missing. Leaving that box empty earns the point.

track_b.title: Penalized omission
track_b.explanation: The same predicted form omits Sam, a reviewer named in this scenario.

track_b.title: Inactive entry
track_b.explanation: Selecting No makes details inactive. Submitting Broken latch adds one extra entry.

track_b.title: Unknown entry with a predicted region
track_b.explanation: C-17 appears in a predicted box below the date. That field has no reference match.

track_b.title: Unknown entry without a region
track_b.explanation: The submission includes case_number, but the supplied spec gives it no box. It still counts as an extra entry.
